tagline: Across the sagebrush to the rim, and two rivers far below.
intro: NM 378 leaves NM 522 north of Questa, runs west through Cerro, and carries on as pavement into the Bureau of Land Management's Wild Rivers Recreation Area, a loop across the sagebrush and piñon-juniper of the Taos Plateau to the rim of the Rio Grande gorge. The gorge is cut through black volcanic rock, 600 to 800 feet deep, with the Sangre de Cristo peaks off to the east.
Down at the bottom the Rio Grande runs rocky and riffling, its upper reaches not yet slowed by dams and diversions. In 1968 it was among the first eight rivers Congress named Wild and Scenic.

moments.title: Cerro
moments.text: Settlers from Taos and Questa founded Cerro in 1854 and named it for Cerro Guadalupe, and the thermometer here has twice gone to 34 below.

moments.title: La Junta Point
moments.text: From a rim overlook a wheelchair can reach, the Red River can be seen coming into the Rio Grande 800 feet below.

moments.title: Wild Rivers Visitor Center
moments.text: The loop passes the visitor center, whose mural was painted by a group of New Mexico artists with a shared passion for the area and its wildlife.

practical: The recreation area is open all year, and snow is possible from November through March.
